newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM-KYMMENE DECLINES COMMENT ON REPAP.
newsitem.headline: UPM-KYMMENE DECLINES COMMENT ON REPAP.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group UPM-Kymmene on Tuesday declined to comment on a newspaper report which said it was likely to bid for Canadian Repap should Canadian Avenor plans to merge with Repap fail.
The two Canadian forestry groups' shareholders are due to decide on a merger proposal on Wednesday.

Daily Kauppalehti on Tuesday quoted an unnamed UPM source as saying it was likely that UPM would bid for Repap if the planned $1.9 billion merger failed, and said UPM had already offered to buy the indebted Repap group at the end of last year.
"We have no comment on this," UPM chief spokesman Markku Franssila told Reuters by telephone. He also declined to say whether UPM had made an offer last year.
"We are following the situation, like you, from the newspapers," he said.
UPM has said it may be looking to grow in the U.S. and Asia towards the end of this decade by buying existing capacity rather than through greenfield operations.
"With the situation in Europe as it is, any such growth is likely to be elsewhere," Franssila said but noted that this had nothing to do with the Repap situation.
UPM is the world's leading coated magazine paper producer with an annual capacity of 1.8 million tonnes and light-weight-coated (LWC) paper is the group's largest product.

Repap's past strategy to buy undervalued paper and pulp mills and modernise them with debt financing had given it modern machinery and a leading position in light-weight-coated paper in North America, Kauppalehti said.
Repap's downsides are its debts and pulp production, it said.
